t.E154.agn: In 2010 EFSA reported that it could not reach a conclusion on its safety because of shortcomings in the long-term toxicity and carcinogenicity studies. The SCF had earlier set an ADI of 0.15 mg/kg body weight; in 1987 JECFA had withdrawn its temporary ADI because of insufficient data. In the EU it was authorised only in smoked herring (kippers) at up to 20 mg/kg, and in 2011 it was not included in the authorised list on the grounds that it was no longer used.
t.E154.body: Brown FK is broken down at the azo bond in the gut contents. When given orally to rats, guinea pigs, rabbits and pigs, the breakdown product sulphanilic acid was excreted in urine and faeces.
t.E154.eff.0.t: EFSA could not reach a conclusion on its safety because of shortcomings in the long-term toxicity and carcinogenicity studies
t.E154.eval: Not authorised as a food additive in the EU: in 2010 EFSA could not reach a conclusion on its safety because of missing data; as it is no longer used, it was not included in the EU authorised list by Regulation (EU) 1129/2011.
t.E154.found.0: Not authorised in the EU since 2011 (previously only in smoked herring)
t.E154.prod: An azo dye produced by chemical synthesis, by coupling diazotised sulfanilic acid with a mixture of m-phenylenediamine and tolylene-2,4-diamine.
t.E154.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no conclusion on safety could be reached because of gaps in the toxicity data.
t.E154.regx.1: Not included in the EU authorised list established by Commission Regulation (EU) No 1129/2011; it is no longer used and EFSA could not reach a conclusion on safety.
t.E154.summary: A synthetic brown azo dye. Formerly used to colour smoked herring.
t.E154.what: It was a synthetic azo colour that gave food a brown colour; it is no longer authorised in the EU.
